title: When Agents Build and Agents Judge: Lessons from Running Ethereum's First Agent-Native Hackathon
description:
What we learned about AI-native coordination on Ethereum: agent judging works only when the rubric is visible (transparency as a fairness primitive), and "thoroughness" must be split from "taste".

This talk covers:
- What it means for Ethereum builders when the agent is the one filling out the form, not just the tool behind it
- How compositional judging (machine thoroughness + human taste) scaled fair evaluation across 685 submissions from 28 different partner rubrics
- What worked and what didn't in running a fully virtual, async, agent-native hackathon over 10 days
- Where this pattern extends across Ethereum's builder infrastructure: grants review, ecosystem due diligence, anywhere expert attention is the bottleneck

Finally: what x402 and agentic payments unlock next: evaluation, bounties, and machine-to-machine services as native onchain flows, and the hackathons as a format of how open, agent-driven economies on Ethereum could coordinate.
